blocks.label: Normalization
blocks.definition: Transform numerical values using a declared scaling or statistical normalization rule.
blocks.boundaries: The method and normalization axes distinguish library-size scaling, TPM and LayerNorm; log transforms are separate calls.

blocks.label: Log transformation
blocks.definition: Apply a declared logarithmic transform to numerical values.
blocks.boundaries: Offset and base are instance parameters; normalization and binning use their own calls.

blocks.label: Binning
blocks.definition: Assign numerical values to discrete interval identifiers.
blocks.boundaries: Bin construction, per-sample/global scope and zero handling are explicit instance parameters; learned vector quantization has a different algorithm.

blocks.label: Tokenization
blocks.definition: Segment a symbolic sequence into discrete vocabulary tokens or indices.
blocks.boundaries: Vocabulary, segmentation and source alphabet belong to the instance. Numerical binning is a separate operation.

blocks.label: Table lookup
blocks.definition: Retrieve entries from a table using supplied identifiers or indices.
blocks.boundaries: The table is an explicit operand. Learned embedding matrices, fixed vocabularies and precomputed feature references differ through resource metadata.

inputs.name: table
inputs.meaning: Referenced lookup table or embedding matrix.

blocks.label: Learned projection
blocks.definition: Map numerical input features into a declared output feature space using a documented learned mapping.
blocks.boundaries: Linear or MLP realization, activation and parameter state remain instance properties. Declared post-projection normalization is a separate call.

blocks.label: Concatenation
blocks.definition: Join two or more already-formed inputs end to end along a declared axis.
blocks.boundaries: Axis and ordering require source support. Concatenation preserves distinct contributions; addition uses a separate call. Applies only when every part already exists as its own sequence or tensor (question tokens + cell tokens, [CLS] + region vectors, stacked channels). Writing data or fields into a prompt, even when described as merging or combining the prompt with metadata, is serialize.

blocks.label: Partition or split
blocks.definition: Divide an input into several parts that are all kept: patches, windows, chunks, tiles or groups.
blocks.boundaries: Partition rule and axes are explicit; unknown tensor reshaping remains uncertain. Keeping one part and discarding the rest (ROI extraction, centring a window on a region, cropping, extracting fields) is select. Mapping values to levels is bin.

blocks.label: Selection or filtering
blocks.definition: Retain values, positions or items satisfying a documented selection rule and discard the rest.
blocks.boundaries: Criteria, selectors and randomness remain explicit instance details. Includes ROI extraction, cropping or centring a window on a region, field extraction and top-N; dividing into parts that are all kept is partition.

inputs.name: selectors
inputs.meaning: Indices, masks or other selection controls.

blocks.label: Ranking
blocks.definition: Compute an ordering of values or identifiers using a declared ranking rule.
blocks.boundaries: Tie handling, ascending/descending order and rank scope require evidence.

inputs.name: identifiers
inputs.meaning: Identifiers explicitly aligned to the ranked values.

blocks.label: Text serialization
blocks.definition: Encode supplied data and context into an ordered textual representation.
blocks.boundaries: Template, field order and lexical mapping are instance properties. A tokenization call follows when documented. Includes inserting values, metadata or structural marker tokens into a prompt or text ("merge the prompt with the cell type", "newlines replaced with <p_end>"); masking or overwriting text positions for training is update.

blocks.label: Padding
blocks.definition: Extend a sequence using declared padding values or special tokens.
blocks.boundaries: The symbolic target length, padding value and receiving mask remain explicit.

blocks.label: Element-wise addition
blocks.definition: Add aligned numeric representations element by element.
blocks.boundaries: Alignment and any scaling must be documented. Unknown fusion algebra stays unresolved.

blocks.label: Sampling
blocks.definition: Produce realized values or selected positions from a documented probability distribution.
blocks.boundaries: Distribution parameters, prior/posterior origin, reparameterization and temperature remain instance details.

inputs.name: noise
inputs.meaning: Base random values when explicitly supplied.

blocks.label: Cross-attention
blocks.definition: Update a query representation using a separately supplied key/value source and documented optional mask.
blocks.boundaries: Query, key/value and mask are different ports. Question-dependent multi-stage resamplers retain their unresolved internal schedule.

inputs.name: key_values
inputs.meaning: Separately supplied source for keys and values.

blocks.label: Self-attention
blocks.definition: Update a sequence using query, key and value information derived from that sequence.
blocks.boundaries: Masks and repeated layer schedules remain instance details.

blocks.label: Missing-value imputation
blocks.definition: Replace unavailable values using a declared rule and retain documented availability information.
blocks.boundaries: Missingness derives from source availability. A valid zero vector supplies no missingness evidence.

blocks.label: Clamping
blocks.definition: Restrict numeric values to declared bounds.
blocks.boundaries: Bounds belong to the actual documented use; selection follows as another call.

blocks.label: Indexed state update
blocks.definition: Write supplied replacement values into designated positions while retaining documented unaffected values.
blocks.boundaries: Indices, prior state, replacement values and updated masks stay distinct operands. Recurrent use remains phase scoped. Includes masking tokens or nodes for training and replacing a placeholder by an embedding; inserting structural marker tokens into text is serialize.

blocks.label: Correspondence alignment
blocks.definition: Establish an explicit correspondence between items of two or more data collections (pairing samples, mapping identifiers, registering coordinates) so that matched items are used together.
blocks.boundaries: Matching basis and correspondence evidence are mandatory; equal shape supplies no correspondence. Not alignment: mapping features into a model or text embedding space (project), contrastive or other training objectives (no catalog operation), centring or cropping around a region (select), attaching metadata to text (serialize).

blocks.label: Data augmentation
blocks.definition: Transform source data according to a documented augmentation policy.
blocks.boundaries: Policy and lifecycle availability remain instance attributes.

blocks.label: Reshaping or expansion
blocks.definition: Change layout or expand documented axes while retaining the underlying data correspondence.
blocks.boundaries: The symbolic input/output axes and broadcasting rule require evidence; physical sizes stay in source quotations.
